address.description: Date when the employee was created in the system.

clients.description: List of employee's clients, if any

fullyEvaluated.description: Number of people that were fully evaluated.

noEvaluated.description: Number of people that were not evaluated.

partiallyEvaluated.description: Number of people that were partially evaluated.

FeedbackReport.description: Personal feedback report: the report for an evaluated in an specific appraisal.

hasReport.description: To know if the evaluated has a report

percentageAchievedObjectives.description: Percentage of achieved objectives by the evaluated

positionCode.description: Job position's code of the evaluated

positionId.description: Job position's ID of the evaluated

seniority.description: Years that the evaluated has been working in the company

total.description: Number of feedback reports contained in the collection list

employees.description: List of employees with a file

surveysReviewedNumber.description: Number of surveys that the employee has reviewed

info.description:
Welcome to the HRider API! This API follows the HAL (Hypertext Application Language) standard and has been dessigned following the HATEOAS (Hypermedia as the Engine of Application State) principle. That makes a simple and consistent way to use the API and discover all its potential by following the links that each resource provides. Below you will find all the available resources and the models the API works with. To try the examples, you need an **API Key** to pass the authorization filters. *HRider uses 64-bit numbers for identifiers. Since the maximum number that can be represented in javascript is 2 ^ 53 - 1, the IDs that appear when performing the tests from this page **may be displayed incorrectly**. Use CURL or an equivalent tool to get the correct data. Making a call from this page will show you the code of the equivalent call in CURL with the necessary parameters.*

CURL example to get root resource:

curl -X GET 'https://dev.hrider.net/api/v1' -H 'authorization: bearer **YOUR-API-KEY**'

Notes and conventions used in the API:
  • Atrributes use lower case
  • Dates must be an UTC 'yyyy-mm-ddTHH:MMZ'. E.g. **2019-10-31T23:00Z**
  • When an endpoint expects a ''text/uri-list'' as a body to identify one or more resources the system allows cutting the URI specifying only the ID. For example, a line with only the employee ID: ''123'', is equivalent to a line with the full URI: ''/companies/100/employees/123''
  • **_embedded** and **_links** properties are read-only for all API objects in the model. You don't need to include them in a POST O PUT call
